svg.title: Where the Captive Health Dollar Sits
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-captive-dollar-comparison; chapter number: 4; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Where the Captive Health Dollar Sits; subtitle: Spend shares, loss-fund cession, and member loss ratio; total range: Percent shares on the bases noted for each bucket; caption: Shopping stop-loss each year attacks only about a fifth of total health spend, while captive members cede most of premium to a shared loss fund and see dollars returned.; assumptions note: Buckets use different bases. The first two are shares of total employer health spend, the third is a share of captive premium, and the fourth is the captive loss ratio.; note: Sources are Joe Perelli of Captive Resources and CRI results reported on the Christopher Martens panel.; buckets: label: Below-Deductible Claims; low: 75; high: 80; notes: Share of total health spend the employer retains under the specific deductible.; label: Stop-Loss Premium; low: 15; high: 20; notes: Share of total health spend, the only slice an annual stop-loss shop touches.; label: Premium Ceded to Member Loss Fund; low: 60; high: 65; notes: Share of captive premium ceded to the member loss fund in CRI programs.; label: Captive Loss Ratio; low: 93; high: 101; notes: CRI results alongside $35M returned to members over 10 years.
